This reduces to the standard isotropic subspace; the remaining symplectic matrix is a linear substitution followed by a symmetric shear. Reversing these steps gives the required operations. Each preserves Schwartz–Bruhat functions. For a partial Fourier interchange, enlarge the support and period denominator to a common integer R.
